findings.fault: The 'Vibe' heading is underlined, italic and in the turquoise link colour, so it looks like a link. It is static text and tapping it does nothing. Its sibling heading 'Surf' is plain ink, so the visitor has no other reason why 'Vibe' would look different.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker scanning on a phone would tap 'Vibe' to find nightlife or social detail, and nothing would happen. That costs them a tap and some trust that the page's links work. It also takes the link's reserved underline and colour for a heading.

findings.where: Good for: all twelve tags (First-time surfers through Sunsets)
findings.fault: These static facts are drawn as filled, outlined pills with a strong edge, the shape of a selectable filter chip or a button. They are not acted on. Each pill also takes a different, apparently random fill and edge colour (amber, green, coral, teal, purple, pink), so colour looks as if it codes a category or state when it codes nothing.
findings.who_objects: On a hostel-search brand, a backpacker expects pills under 'Good for' to filter hostels, so they tap 'Remote workers' or 'Budget' and nothing happens. Varied colours also make them look for a meaning that isn't there. The chip shape is reserved for selection, and the colours read as a status code.

findings.where: The coming-soon announcement block below 'What to look for'
findings.fault: A neutral notice about Manta's launch sits on a saturated red ground, the look of an error or failure alert. The page is telling the visitor something calm, that listings are coming soon, in the colour reserved for errors and sold-out states.
findings.who_objects: A visitor would read the red box as an error, such as the page failing to load listings or Canggu being unavailable, before reading the words. That gives a wrong impression on a page meant to reassure. It also weakens red's meaning for real errors and sold-out rows on the rest of the site.

findings.where: Header: wordmark home link, 'Destinations' and 'How we rank'. Footer: 'Privacy', 'Terms', 'How we rank' and 'Report content'
findings.fault: Every navigation link except the email goes nowhere. The wordmark and 'How we rank' (in both header and footer), 'Privacy', 'Terms' and 'Report content' all link back to this same page. 'Destinations' points to a #destinations anchor, but the page has no such section. The visitor cannot reach the ranking method, the legal pages, a content report or any other destination.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who wants to know how Manta ranks hostels, or wants to compare Canggu with another Bali stop, clicks and lands where they started. To a first-time visitor, a ranking-trust link and legal links that go nowhere make the site look unfinished. A visitor who needs to report content has no way to do it from the page.

findings.where: End of the page: the coming-soon block and what follows it
findings.fault: The page ends with no next step. Listings are 'coming soon', but there is no way to be told when they arrive and no link to other destinations or to the guide's own advice. A visitor who decides Canggu suits them has nothing to act on except the footer's dead links.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker planning their next hop who is convinced by the guide leaves with nothing to do here and goes to an OTA to book. For a pre-launch product, losing that visitor with no way to return is the page's main missed job.
